title: An Open Evaluation-Tampering Detection Dataset and Scorer

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: manual transcript review does not scale. An automated evaluation-tampering scorer enables large-scale monitoring of agentic systems, directly improving practical safety coverage.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires training a classifier on MALT annotations, running agentic tasks to generate new transcripts, and measuring precision/recall. This is advanced ML pipeline work for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: training classifier on existing annotations, generating new agent transcripts, and evaluating detection performance. Each step is well-defined but the full pipeline is substantial for 30 hours.

evidence: METR published the MALT dataset (Oct 2025) with 10,919 agent transcripts and fine-grained labels for reward hacking and sandbagging, plus basic prompted monitors achieving AUROCs of 0.96 and 0.91.
MALT already includes a monitoring baseline that uses transcript chunking with JSON-output classification scores, reaching 80-90% true positive rates at 5% false positive rate.
Redwood Research published 'Benchmarks for Detecting Measurement Tampering' with evaluation of detection techniques on dedicated datasets.

The proposed project adds value by building a dedicated open dataset and scorer specifically for evaluation-tampering detection (beyond MALT's broader scope), but the core infrastructure (labeled transcripts, basic monitoring) already exists.
